dimensions.name: Construct validity
dimensions.question: Does performance on the eval validly measure the capability or behaviour the eval aims to assess?

contributions.name: measurement distortion
contributions.definition: flaws in implementation validity dimensions distort measurement of the target construct

contributions.name: contamination
contributions.definition: benchmark items or their solutions were present in training data or otherwise accessible during training

contributions.name: memorisation
contributions.definition: performance depends on recalling a memorised solution rather than exercising the intended capability

contributions.name: eval awareness
contributions.definition: models recognise the evaluation context and alter their behaviour as a result

contributions.name: sandbagging
contributions.definition: models deliberately or strategically underperform relative to their capability

contributions.name: confounds
contributions.definition: scores are systematically affected by factors unrelated to the target construct

contributions.name: proxy measurement
contributions.definition: the measured outcome is only an imperfect proxy for the target capability or behaviour

contributions.name: capability vs propensity
contributions.definition: the evaluation conflates what a model can do with what it tends to do

dimensions.name: Content validity
dimensions.question: Do the tasks adequately represent the target domain and situations the evaluation aims to cover?

contributions.name: coverage gaps
contributions.definition: important parts of the target domain or capability are absent or underrepresented

contributions.name: unrepresentative task distribution
contributions.definition: the distribution of tasks differs materially from the target domain

dimensions.name: Task Specification
dimensions.question: Are individual tasks correctly specified, solvable, and free from defects that affect performance?

contributions.name: incorrect reference answer
contributions.definition: the reference answer is incorrect or inconsistent with the task

contributions.name: impossible tasks
contributions.definition: no correct answer is attainable as posed

contributions.name: missing information
contributions.definition: required parameters or context are not supplied

contributions.name: guessability
contributions.definition: tasks can be solved using superficial cues rather than the intended competence

contributions.name: prompt defects
contributions.definition: the prompts are ambiguous, incomplete, misleading, or otherwise fail to specify correctly what the model should do

contributions.name: hidden requirements
contributions.definition: success depends on unstated conventions or assumptions

contributions.name: unintended shortcuts
contributions.definition: answers are reachable without performing the intended work

dimensions.name: Scaffolding
dimensions.question: Does the scaffolding provide the model with an appropriate setup for performing the task?

contributions.name: system prompt issues
contributions.definition: system-level instructions are ambiguous, misleading, or otherwise distort performance

contributions.name: planning or agent loop
contributions.definition: the agent structure constrains or alters performance

contributions.name: memory & context strategy
contributions.definition: the strategy for retaining and presenting context loses or obscures information needed to solve the task

contributions.name: retry/error feedback
contributions.definition: failures are surfaced poorly or recovery opportunities are handled inconsistently

contributions.name: coaching
contributions.definition: the scaffolding provides hints or information that artificially improves performance

dimensions.name: Harness
dimensions.question: Does the evaluation infrastructure correctly execute the specified task and scaffolding?

contributions.name: tool-call handling
contributions.definition: tool calls are parsed, routed, or executed incorrectly

contributions.name: submission/termination logic
contributions.definition: episodes terminate earlier or later than intended

contributions.name: context delivery
contributions.definition: task materials or interaction history reach the model incompletely

contributions.name: message handling
contributions.definition: messages are truncated, reordered, duplicated, or otherwise mishandled

contributions.name: state management
contributions.definition: evaluation state is lost, corrupted, or inconsistently maintained

contributions.name: harness bugs
contributions.definition: other defects in the evaluation infrastructure affect performance

contributions.name: harness sensitivity
contributions.definition: results change materially across equivalent harnesses

dimensions.name: Environment
dimensions.question: Does the task environment and its resources function as specified?

contributions.name: tool failures
contributions.definition: tools error, malfunction, or hang during episodes

contributions.name: missing resources
contributions.definition: files, packages, or services assumed by the task are absent

contributions.name: broken files & dependencies
contributions.definition: inputs or dependencies are corrupt, incompatible, or unreadable

contributions.name: non-determinism
contributions.definition: the environment varies between otherwise equivalent runs

contributions.name: information leakage
contributions.definition: the environment exposes answers or unintended hints

contributions.name: implementation differs from specification
contributions.definition: the environment behaves differently from its documented design

dimensions.name: Grading
dimensions.question: Does the grading procedure correctly determine whether task performance satisfies the evaluation criteria?

contributions.name: false positives and false negatives
contributions.definition: the grading procedure incorrectly classifies responses as satisfying or failing the evaluation criteria

contributions.name: underspecified criteria
contributions.definition: the grading criteria do not clearly determine what counts as satisfying them

contributions.name: judge errors
contributions.definition: LLM judges make systematic, inconsistent, or otherwise erroneous grading decisions

contributions.name: surface-form sensitivity
contributions.definition: otherwise equivalent responses receive different scores because of differences in wording, formatting, or presentation

contributions.name: incorrect partial credit
contributions.definition: partial scores do not appropriately reflect the quality or correctness of the response

contributions.name: grader exploitation
contributions.definition: submissions can manipulate or exploit the grading procedure

dimensions.name: Resource limits
dimensions.question: Do resource constraints provide an appropriate opportunity for models to perform on the task?

contributions.name: turn/token/time limits
contributions.definition: limits terminate productive attempts before the model can complete the task

contributions.name: resource sensitivity
contributions.definition: performance changes materially with the available resource budget

contributions.name: unequal constraint effects
contributions.definition: the same nominal constraint binds models differently

dimensions.name: Informativeness
dimensions.question: Does the evaluation provide enough variation and signal to distinguish relevant differences between models?

contributions.name: saturation
contributions.definition: frontier models cluster at the attainable ceiling, limiting the benchmark's ability to distinguish between them

contributions.name: floor/ceiling effects
contributions.definition: the attainable score range compresses meaningful differences between models

contributions.name: clustering
contributions.definition: model scores cluster tightly relative to measurement uncertainty, providing little discriminative power between models
